title: Homogeneous systems and affine solution spaces
section: Gaussian Elimination ▷ Free Variables and Homogeneous Systems
terms: free variable; parameter; homogeneous system; nonhomogeneous system; trivial solution; particular solution; general solution; affine solution space.

exposition.text:
A homogeneous system is Ax = 0 and always has the trivial solution x = 0. Its solutions form a
vector space. If a system Ax = b is consistent and x is one particular solution, every solution is
p
x = x + x , where Ax = 0.
p h h
With n unknowns and coefficient rank r, a consistent system has n − r independent free parame-
ters. A nonhomogeneous solution set is a translate of a nullspace and is usually an affine space
rather than a vector subspace. Differences of solutions are homogeneous solutions; sums of two
solutions generally solve Ax = 2b, not Ax = b.
When b ̸= 0, the linear span of the nonempty affine solution set has dimension dim ker A + 1,
because a particular solution lies outside the kernel. The solution of least Euclidean norm is
characterized by being perpendicular to every homogeneous direction; adding a perpendicular
direction would increase its squared norm.

question.text:
A real 4 × 7 matrix has rank 3, and Ax = b is consistent. What is the dimension of its affine
solution set?
(A) 1 (B) 2 (C) 3 (D) 4 (E) 7

solution.text:
The directions in the solution set form ker A, whose dimension is number of columns minus
rank, 7 − 3 = 4. The number of equations is not the number of independent constraints.

question.text:
The solutions of a consistent real system are x = (1, 2, 0) + t(1, −1, 1), t ∈ R. Which value of t
gives the solution of least Euclidean norm?
(A) −1 (B) −1/3 (C) 0 (D) 1/3 (E) 1

solution.text:
2 2 2 2
The squared norm is (1 + t) + (2 − t) + t = 5 − 2t + 3t , minimized at
t = 1/3. Equivalently the minimizing solution is perpendicular to the homogeneous direc-
tion (1, −1, 1). Minimizing the norm is the same as minimizing its square.

question.text:
A real 3 × 5 matrix A has rank three, and b ̸= 0. What is the dimension of the linear span of all
solutions of Ax = b?
(A) 1 (B) 2 (C) 3 (D) 4 (E) 5

solution.text:
The solution set is x +ker A, with nullity two. Its linear span is span{x }+ker A: differences
